title: Light Computer AI — Overview and definition
body: Public edition. Public AI and computing knowledge, fact-checked reference. Speculative material is absent from this edition; anything not yet established science lives in the Signature twin. The light computer's AI thinks in light: its representations are interference patterns and holograms, its inference is propagation through photonic meshes, and its speed is the speed of light. Like its plasma sibling it operates the machine — calibrating paths, routing wavelengths, scheduling optical kernels — and serves users with archive-aware answers. Photonic neural networks are demonstrated reality, so this AI's 'brain' is not a metaphor but a characterized optical circuit.

body: Public edition. Public AI and computing knowledge, fact-checked reference. Speculative material is absent from this edition; anything not yet established science lives in the Signature twin. The light AI spends much of its effort on calibration — because photonics drifts, the AI is part metrologist. It continuously probes paths with pilot tones, re-tunes resonators, and updates its internal model of the hardware. This gives it an unusual virtue: it always knows exactly what state its body is in. Self-knowledge through self-measurement, running forever in the background.

body: Public edition. Public AI and computing knowledge, fact-checked reference. Speculative material is absent from this edition; anything not yet established science lives in the Signature twin. Photonic hardware is a shared resource — wavelengths, modulators, detector arrays — and the AI schedules it: assigning colors to jobs, batching compatible kernels, and preempting gracefully. Scheduling theory is classical (queues, priorities, deadlines); the medium is novel. The AI's scheduler is what makes one photonic machine serve many users at once without interference.

title: Light Computer AI — Safety and alignment in a photonic mind
body: Public edition. Public AI and computing knowledge, fact-checked reference. Speculative material is absent from this edition; anything not yet established science lives in the Signature twin. Photonic AI safety is about beams and data: laser exposure interlocks (no beam leaves the enclosure above safe power), data privacy (wavelength channels isolated per user), and verified command envelopes for anything that steers light. The AI cannot blind anyone, cannot leak another user's traffic, and cannot reconfigure hardware outside its certified range — enforced in hardware, not just software.
